title: An Agent's strategy lives in the non-Primitive residual branch while the Primitive tree holds only its capabilities
content:
A.6.1.1.5.3.2 — **Strategic Intent And Operating Model** — sits inside Omni Documents, the branch defined as covering "infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activities unrelated to Sky Primitives, or activities spanning multiple Sky Primitives." It states that "Obex is an incubation-focused Prime … It provides capital, infrastructure, and technical support to early-stage teams building on Sky Primitives," and carries the Operating Model, Risk and Compliance, Accord Alignment, First-Loss and Recourse Principles, and Transparency Standards.

So the Agent's purpose is documented *outside* the Primitive tree. Everything under A.6.1.1.5.2 describes mechanism — which Primitives are active, what functions exist, what limits apply — and none of it says why. The answer to "what is this Agent for?" is in the residual bucket, because incubation is an activity the Sky Primitive catalogue has no Primitive for.

That placement is coherent given how Omni Documents are defined, and it explains why the Primitive sections read as capability inventories: the framework standardises *how* Agents act so those actions can be governed uniformly, and leaves *what they are trying to achieve* to per-Agent prose.

The consequence for a reader is a specific reading order. The Primitive tree tells you an Agent's risk surface and permissions with precision; Omni Documents tell you its intent with no structural enforcement at all. Obex's most consequential business commitments — first-loss exposure, enforceable recourse, published default rates — are in the half of the document that has no Invocation process, no lifecycle branches, and no Instance-level review.
description: Obex's mandate, operating model, first-loss principles and transparency standards all sit under Omni Documents, so the Primitive sections describe what the Agent can do rather than what it intends.
